summary: Umpawaug Hill lookout in West Redding: a steel tower completed in 1936, with observers in 1942 and 1966; no source says what the site is like now.

facts.design: Steel tower with a cabin floor 62 feet (18.9 m) above the ground

events.note: Steel tower completed in 1936, per a 1942 newspaper item quoted on the page; the page says the Civilian Conservation Corps built it
Observer spotted and reported grass fires in Ridgefield and reported a grass fire in the Florida district; the item is dated April 30, 1942
Observer on duty 45 hours a week from March; the item describes her as an employee of the Park and Forest commission

evidence.supports: lookout on Umpawaug Hill in West Redding
evidence.quote: observer at the Redding fire tower atop Umpawaug Hill in West Redding

evidence.supports: built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
evidence.quote: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: steel tower completed 1936 and used annually since; cabin floor 62 ft above ground
evidence.quote: The spotting platform elevation is 744 feet above sea level, the cabin floor being 62 feet above the ground at the top of the steel tower completed in 1936 and used annually since.

evidence.supports: observer on duty 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily in fire season
evidence.quote: The observer is on duty at the tower from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily during the forest fire season.

evidence.supports: 1942 grass fires in Ridgefield spotted and reported by observer
evidence.quote: Two of three grass fires in Ridgefield Sunday were spotted and reported within a few hundred feet by Mrs. Russell Hoddinott

evidence.supports: 1942 grass fire in Florida district reported by tower
evidence.quote: The Redding tower also reported a grass fire later in the afternoon on property of A. C. Iser in Florida district.
Visitors are always welcome at the Redding fire tower.
The 52 foot perch is a seasonal job

evidence.supports: 1966 observer described as an employee of the Park and Forest commission

evidence.quote: A short wave radio keeps her in touch with Connecticut's 14 fire towers.

corrections.current: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps.
corrections.why: The agency field holds a build credit, not an agency. The 1966 item ties the observer to the Park and Forest commission, and the Painter Hill page names it the Connecticut Park and Forest Commission. No source here names who owned this tower, so a human should confirm before applying.

notes_for_editor: One source only: a compiled Forest Lookouts page quoting a 1942 Ridgefield Press item and a 1966 Bridgeport Post item. Nothing says what became of the tower after 1966, what it is like today, or whether the site is open; the story says so. Height conflict: the 1942 item gives 62 ft to the cabin floor, the 1966 item a 52 ft perch; facts use 18.9 m from 1942 and the story gives both figures. Build date: the page gives no year for the CCC build, only the 1936 steel tower. Record elevation 225 m is close to the 744 ft (226.8 m) spotting-platform figure in the 1942 item. Our crawl catalogs (NHLR, FFLOS, CT list) have no Umpawaug entry. Two web searches found nothing on the tower. The brief's 'agency' correction is proposed, not applied.
